adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:91 — update() evaluates the login predicate on the org-aware wrapped model from getById (isEnabled=false when org or realm organizations are disabled), so an update making an org IDP hideOnLogin/linkOnly/non-public while its org is disabled skips invalidation and the stale ID reappears on login once the org is re-enabled (bean only re-checks isEnabled).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows update() calling getById() and then registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), but it does not show that getById() returns an “org-aware wrapped model” or that such a wrapper forces isEnabled=false when organizations are disabled. The alleged skip in invalidation depends on that unstated behavior. Also, invalidationOnUpdate only skips when BOTH original and updated fail getLoginPredicate(), which is not demonstrably caused by this diff (updated is the passed-in model, not necessarily wrapped). Therefore the finding’s described stale-cache scenario is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:80 — The bean re-checks only isEnabled on cached results, so any cached entry that no longer meets hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC is shown on the login page instead of being filtered out.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the login-page list is obtained via `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)`, which is filtered by `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` (now also checks `BROKER_PUBLIC` for org-linked IDPs). The PR adds caching + targeted invalidation (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) designed to clear caches whenever an IDP’s “available for login” status changes (e.g., hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC/org link changes), and the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` explicitly exercises `hideOnLogin` and org-link/BROKER_PUBLIC changes and expects caches to be invalidated. The bean’s added `idp.isEnabled()` filter is a defensive re-check, but the claim that cached entries failing hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC will be shown is not supported by the diff because those changes should invalidate the cache and `getForLogin`’s predicate should exclude them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:381 — Cleanup (lines 381, 425; copied from 303) registers get("alias")::remove (a literal alias) instead of the created alias, so the 21 test IDPs are never removed and leak into later tests.

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:400 — The test only checks that cache entries exist or are null and counts the IDs; it never compares a cache-hit getForLogin result with the delegate result and never covers login-IDP removal or disabled orgs, so stale-cache bugs would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` largely validates cache population/invalidation by asserting `IdentityProviderListQuery` presence/absence and the size of cached internal-id sets (e.g., `assertEquals(..., identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(...).size())`). It does not assert that a subsequent `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` call returns the same IDPs as the delegate/non-cached path (i.e., it doesn’t validate correctness on cache hits beyond counts), and it doesn’t cover removal of an IDP that *does* qualify for login (it only removes `idp-alias-1`, which is disabled by construction). The “disabled orgs” part isn’t exercised in this diff either. This is a concrete gap in testing newly added caching logic, but not a verifiable product defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:502 — Step 4 runs an update and addIdentityProvider before a single assertion, so it cannot show whether the org-link change (not the first update) caused the invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In Step 4 of `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the test performs two state-changing operations back-to-back (`update(idpRep)` to set `BROKER_PUBLIC`, then `addIdentityProvider("idp-alias-20")`) and only then asserts that the login caches were invalidated. Since there is no assertion/checkpoint between these calls, the test cannot isolate which operation caused the invalidation it observes, reducing the test's ability to specifically validate that the org-link change triggers invalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — Public SPI getLoginPredicate() now also requires BROKER_PUBLIC for org-linked IDPs via an ad-hoc clause outside the LoginFilter enum, so it silently diverges from getLoginSearchOptions() and changes semantics for any third-party caller (no in-repo callers besides the new Infinispan code).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` now adds an extra condition (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`) outside the `LoginFilter` enum’s composed filters, while `getLoginSearchOptions()` is still driven by the enum. This creates a real semantic divergence between the predicate and the enum-derived search options, and it changes behavior for any external/third-party callers of the public SPI predicate (whether or not there are other in-repo callers can’t be verified from the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:244 — Cached getForLogin collects IDs into a HashSet and returns HashSet order, dropping the delegate's result ordering (and REALM-then-ORG grouping for ALL), so callers other than the sorting IDP bean may see nondeterministic order.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added cached path for `getForLogin(...)`, IDs are gathered into a `Set` (`cached` is a `Set<String>` via `Collectors.toSet()`), then models are accumulated into `Set<IdentityProviderModel> identityProviders = new HashSet<>();` and returned as `identityProviders.stream()`. This loses any ordering from the delegate stream and makes the result order dependent on `HashSet` iteration order, which can differ from the non-cached path (`return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(...)`). The diff doesn’t show an explicit ordering contract for `getForLogin`, so it’s not provably a functional bug, but it is a concrete behavior change/inconsistency introduced by this diff that could affect callers relying on stable/grouped ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75 — getForLogin can return org-aware wrapped IDPs whose isEnabled() is false (disabled org), contradicting the SPI javadoc promise that returned IDPs are enabled; only this caller was patched to re-check instead of fixing the provider contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only the FreeMarker bean caller being patched to add an extra `idp.isEnabled()` filter, with an explicit comment: `// re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped.` (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java). The PR does not adjust the `getForLogin(...)` implementations/providers to enforce that returned IDPs are enabled, so other callers could still observe disabled/wrapped IDPs. However, the claim about an SPI javadoc promise is not shown in the diff, and the provider-side behavior (“can return … isEnabled() false”) is implied but not strictly proven here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:77 — New public static cacheKeyForLogin(RealmModel, FetchMode) exposes internal cache-key format as API solely for tests; it bakes FetchMode.toString() into the key.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new `public static String cacheKeyForLogin(RealmModel realm, FetchMode fetchMode)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` and the new test (`OrganizationCacheTest`) statically imports and uses it, which effectively exposes the cache-key construction outside the cache provider implementation. The key is built via string concatenation with `fetchMode` (`"." + fetchMode`), which relies on `FetchMode`’s string representation (typically `Enum.toString()`/`name()`), making the cache key format more coupled to that enum’s representation. This is an encapsulation/API surface concern, but not a directly verifiable runtime bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — Update-time invalidation evaluates getLoginPredicate on the org-aware wrapped original from getById (isEnabled=false when its org is disabled), so changing hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC to non-login while the org is disabled skips invalidation and the stale cached ID is shown again once the org is re-enabled (the bean only re-checks isEnabled)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows update-time invalidation calling `getById(model.getInternalId())` and then applying `getLoginPredicate()` to `original` and `updated` in `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`. However, the finding’s key premise—that `getById` returns an “org-aware wrapped” model whose `isEnabled` becomes false when the org is disabled—is not evidenced anywhere in this diff (neither `getById` implementation nor such wrapper behavior is shown). adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:384 — The login-cache invalidation predicate (org-aware isEnabled on wrapped models) doesn't match the delegate query that fills the cache (stored ENABLED flag only), so the skip-invalidation shortcuts can leave cached ID sets out of sync with what a fresh query would return

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the login-cache invalidation logic (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) uses the same LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() that conceptually defines “qualifies for login”. The cache itself is populated from idpDelegate.getForLogin(...), and there’s no diff evidence that the delegate query uses a different predicate (e.g., “stored ENABLED flag only”) or that the invalidation predicate is evaluating an “org-aware wrapped” isEnabled that diverges from what getForLogin uses. The only explicit isEnabled re-check is in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (UI filtering) and doesn’t demonstrate a cache invalidation/predicate mismatch in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — The new predicate clause calls idp.getConfig().get(BROKER_PUBLIC) with no null check, so an org-linked model whose config is null throws an NPE from create/update/remove invalidation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` clause `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` with no null-guard on `idp.getConfig()`. New invalidation paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) call this predicate, so if `getConfig()` can ever be null for an org-linked IDP, an NPE would occur. However, the diff does not show whether `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null, so the finding's definite NPE claim is not fully verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:213 — getForLogin copy-pastes the ~40-line cached list-query algorithm from getByOrganization (lines 168-210), differing only in key, searchKey and delegate call; extract a shared helper taking a Supplier<Stream<IdentityProviderModel>>

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new getForLogin(...) implementation that contains a substantial block of cache/list-query logic (creating/reading IdentityProviderListQuery, handling per-searchKey caching, invalidating and repopulating, then resolving IDs back to models) that appears structurally identical to the existing pattern used elsewhere in this class (e.g., getByOrganization, referenced in the finding). adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — Organization-specific BROKER_PUBLIC rule is hardcoded as an ad-hoc lambda in the generic LoginFilter predicate instead of a LoginFilter entry, so getLoginPredicate() and getLoginSearchOptions() no longer describe the same filter

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` now adds an extra organization/BROKER_PUBLIC condition via an inline lambda: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, rather than expressing it as a `LoginFilter` enum entry like the other filters combined from `values()`. The finding’s claim about divergence from `getLoginSearchOptions()` is plausible because only `getLoginPredicate()` changed here (no corresponding change shown for `getLoginSearchOptions()`), creating a potential inconsistency in how “login filters” are described/represented, though the exact `getLoginSearchOptions()` implementation isn’t in the diff to fully prove the mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:403 — registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates getLoginPredicate() on each model twice and builds the predicate four times; compute two booleans once for readability

Since getLoginPredicate() constructs a new predicate each call (see IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() building a composed predicate), this results in rebuilding/evaluating repeatedly. Computing boolean flags once (e.g., originalLoginEligible/updatedLoginEligible) would improve readability and avoid repeated predicate construction, but it’s not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:381 — Cleanup registers get("alias")::remove with a literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias, so the cleanup is dead/ineffective (repeated at line 425; copies pre-existing pattern at line 303)

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (literal string "alias") instead of the created alias. This cleanup will not remove the created IDPs (and likely refers to a non-existent IDP), making the cleanup ineffective. The same incorrect cleanup pattern is repeated when creating `idp-alias-20`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:224 — FetchMode.ALL entry is keyed per organizationId, so each org accumulates its own id set (duplicating all realm-level login IDPs) inside a single cache entry that grows with the number of orgs and is copied on every add.

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin(...)`, the cache key is only `realmId + ".idp.login." + fetchMode` (`cacheKeyForLogin`), so there is a single cache entry per realm+FetchMode. However, the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` is effectively segmented by `searchKey` (`organizationId` or "") via `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` and the constructor `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` when a new org search occurs. This means over time the single cached query can accumulate a separate ID set for each organizationId, and for `FetchMode.ALL` each org-specific set can include the same realm-level login IDPs, duplicating them across many org keys. The code also invalidates/rebuilds the object when a new `searchKey` is introduced, which implies copying/merging prior entries. This is a real, diff-grounded scalability/memory concern, but it’s not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:236 — Each first-seen organization on the login page triggers invalidateObject plus a full re-add of the shared ALL entry (copying all prior search keys), causing cache churn proportional to org count.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added getForLogin() caching logic, the cache key is shared per realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)), while the actual cached IDP sets are segmented by `searchKey` (organizationId or ""). When an `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns null (first time a given orgId is seen), the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then rebuilds and re-adds the entry via `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` (copying prior search keys from `query`). This means each first-seen organization causes an invalidate + full re-add of the shared entry, which is cache churn proportional to distinct orgIds. This is a performance/architecture concern visible in the diff, not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:246 — Cached ids are resolved with per-id getById calls, an N+1 pattern that issues one DB load per IDP on a cold IDP cache for every login page render.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added getForLogin(...) implementation, after obtaining a cached Set<String> of internal IDs, the code iterates `for (String id : cached)` and resolves each entry via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` (see the loop building `identityProviders`). This is a per-ID lookup pattern and can become N+1 work when the list is large and the per-ID lookup is not already warmed/cached. This is a performance/architecture concern introduced by the change rather than a correctness defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:229 — ORG_ONLY with null organizationId (used by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) materializes and caches the unbounded set of all public org IDPs in the realm with no limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds caching for `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`. When `organizationId` is `null`, it uses `searchKey = ""` and eagerly materializes the entire delegate stream into a `Set` (`collect(Collectors.toSet())`) and stores it in `IdentityProviderListQuery` under the single realm+mode cache key (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`). `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` explicitly calls `getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null)` when no org is selected, so this does cache the complete set of qualifying public org-linked IDPs for the realm with no pagination/limit. This is a scalability/performance concern introduced by the new caching behavior, but not a verifiable correctness defect given the API has no limit parameters and is expected to return all login IDPs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:385 — Any create/remove/qualifying update of a login IDP invalidates all FetchMode entries cluster-wide (including per-org data unrelated to the changed IDP), forcing full recomputation for every org.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows login caches are keyed only by realm+FetchMode (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), while per-organization results are stored inside the same `IdentityProviderListQuery` via `searchKey` (orgId or ""). Both `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` (called on create/remove) and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` invalidate *all* modes by looping `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values()) realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode));`. This necessarily clears cached per-org entries unrelated to the changed IDP because they share the same cache key. That’s a breadth/performance/architecture concern evidenced by the code, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — Update-invalidation uses the org-aware wrapped original (isEnabled=false while its org is disabled), so setting hideOnLogin/linkOnly or BROKER_PUBLIC=false on an IDP of a disabled org skips login-cache invalidation and the stale cached id re-exposes the hidden/private broker on login pages once the org is re-enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `update(...)`, the code fetches `idpById = getById(model.getInternalId())` and passes that as the `original` to `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)`. The diff also shows callers may receive an org-aware wrapped IDP whose `isEnabled()` can differ from the underlying model (see the added comment and new `idp.isEnabled()` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`: “idp might have been wrapped”). Since `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` decides to skip invalidation when both `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `.test(updated)` are false, a wrapped `original` that becomes non-login-eligible due solely to org state can cause the method to skip invalidation when updating fields that affect login eligibility (e.g., hide-on-login/link-only filters or the newly added BROKER_PUBLIC constraint in `getLoginPredicate`). This can leave `cacheKeyForLogin(...)` entries populated with stale IDP ids, and once the org state flips back, those stale cached ids can be returned from `getForLogin(...)` without re-filtering, re-exposing an IDP that should no longer qualify for login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:251 — Cache-hit path returns cached IDP ids without re-applying the login predicate (hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC/org match), and callers only re-check isEnabled (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80), so any missed invalidation exposes non-login IDPs on login pages

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached implementation of `getForLogin` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, the cache-hit path rebuilds the result solely from cached internal IDs (`query.getIDPs(searchKey)` then `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`) and does not re-apply `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` or other login-eligibility checks on the returned models. That means correctness relies entirely on the invalidation logic (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). However, the finding’s claim that this *will* expose non-login IDPs is not directly verifiable from the diff because the diff also adds targeted invalidations on create/update/remove and adds tests asserting cache invalidation when login availability changes. So it’s a robustness/defense-in-depth concern grounded in the diff, not a proven defect.
